claims.text:
stage computation: High-dimensional points A=(0,0,0), a=(.1,0,0), B=(0,10,0), b=(.1,10,0), C=(0,0,10), c=(.1,0,10). Compute each point’s unique nearest neighbour. Prescribed2D embedding E1 places the pairs at x=0/.1,5/5.1,10/10.1, all y=0. E2 moves B/b to50/50.1 and C/c to5/5.1. All six nearest-neighbour identities persist while A–B distance changes5→50; original A–B distance remains10.

**Countercase / boundary:** These are deliberately prescribed embeddings, not outputs of a t-SNE/UMAP optimizer and not a proof that every local relation is preserved. Neighbour constraints alone do not identify global spacing. Moving b alone to x=1 breaks its original nearest-neighbour relationship; compute and display that failure too.

**Prediction / transfer recall:** Predict whether the long new A–B gap proves the original points moved; recall that keeping each pair intact but swapping B/C group placement preserves all six1NN identities without recovering original global distances.

**Intervention / reachable witness:** Controls Re-space groups and Break pair recompute a labelled point plot and six-neighbour agreement count. Retain original versus current A–B distance and primary6/6 agreement beside the altered witness; equal plot scales or explicitly labelled x axes are mandatory.
